facts.label: Bottom line

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Loan-sale funding is the dependency that matters most. Gains on loan sales were USD 381 million in Q3 2026, 64.1% of other sales and revenues, which carry a 100% gross margin, and other sales and revenues were 39.4% of gross profit in the nine months to September 2026. Pricing depends on investor demand and credit spreads, so wider spreads would cut gross profit directly. The gain earned per dollar of receivables sold fell from about 10.0% to about 7.4% over the year. Committed capacity is large but finite: the unused commitment of Ally, its committed forward-flow buyer, lasts 9.0 months at the Q3 pace against 9.8 months of remaining term, and USD 8.3 billion of fixed-pool capacity remains. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against treating funding as the weak point is the record of renewal and growth. Ally's commitment to buy loans rose from USD 4.0 billion in January 2025 to USD 6.0 billion in October 2025 and USD 8.0 billion in July 2026, fixed-pool commitments reached USD 12.5 billion, seven receivable facilities are undrawn, USD 13.9 billion of loans were sold in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and the August 2026 refinancing priced a seven-year loan at a lower cost than the notes it replaced. On that record the funding channel has widened as volume grew, and the shock modelled here would need both a market closure and a fall in gains at once. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Scale and growth are the first strength: retail units grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 while the industry was about flat, and Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 2,752 million over the last twelve months, which supports debt service and lets the company spend on capacity from earnings. Low leverage and large cash are the second: debt is 1.90x Adjusted EBITDA and unrestricted cash is USD 3,049 million, so earnings would have to fall far before debt service is threatened. Long-dated first-lien debt is the third: 97.3% of corporate debt falls due in 2031 or later and the Term Loan B ranks pari passu with the 2031 secured notes, so apart from USD 107 million of unsecured notes there is no corporate maturity wall before 2031. Liquidity is the fourth: USD 2,071 million of availability and USD 4,100 million of unused receivable lines against USD 71 million drawn. A supportive record on payouts is the fifth: no dividend and USD 126 million of sponsor equity in 2023. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Carvana is an online used-car retailer that sources, reconditions, finances and delivers vehicles through its own network, and it earns profit from three lines. Retail vehicle sales were 75.4% of nine-month revenue but only 49.5% of gross profit, while other sales and revenues, which are loan-sale gains and commissions with no cost of sales, were 39.4% of gross profit. Cash flow therefore depends on retail volume and on investors buying the loans it originates, which makes visibility shorter than the revenue base suggests, and refinancing confidence rests on loan-sale access as much as on vehicle sales. Retail units grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 while the industry was about flat, according to management. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is volume-driven and discretionary. Retail vehicle sales rose 53.8% in Q3 2026 on 39.4% more units and a higher revenue per unit of USD 28,263 against USD 25,625, a mix of share gains and used-car price appreciation that can reverse. There is no contract revenue: every sale is a one-off transaction with a seven-day return right, and competitors include CarMax, Amazon and DriveTime, which holds a cross-license and could compete. The growth is therefore share gain in a flat industry and not visible recurring revenue, and higher interest rates raise monthly payments and weaken demand. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense but fragmented: the ten largest used-car retailers held less than 10% of the market in 2024 and Carvana has about 2% of it, so share gains can continue, while price competition from CarMax, Amazon and franchise dealers limits margin. New entrants face high operating complexity in reconditioning and logistics, though technology changes such as artificial intelligence and autonomous vehicles are cited as risks to the model. Buyer power is high because switching costs are low and returns are allowed for seven days. Supplier power matters most in funding: vehicles come from customers, auctions and fleets, but Ally and the loan buyers decide how much Carvana can sell, and commercial suppliers review their disposition channels through requests for proposals. facts.label: Credit-translated SWOT
facts.text: Strengths are scale and growth, low leverage with large cash, and long-dated first-lien corporate debt, which together give creditors a margin of safety today. Weaknesses are dependence on loan-sale gains, thinning unit profit, and control and related-party features. The main opportunity is renewal of the 2027 facilities and Ally's commitment on longer terms, which would remove the nearest funding test and lift the profile. The main threats are wider loan-sale spreads, a fall in used-car prices that creates markdown risk on inventory, and a change of control that would accelerate the tax receivable agreement. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale and market position is strong: retail units grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 and the business has about 2% of the used market, which leaves large room for share gains but shows it is far from dominant. Competitive advantage is average: management says its margins are about twice the industry average, but switching costs are low and rivals can copy the online model. Business diversification is weak: a single market, the United States, one online channel and one product category, with other sales and revenues tied to retail units and to loan buyers. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capex is only 0.7% of revenue and advertising can be cut, but the fixed cost share is not disclosed. Margin stability is average: the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 3.1% in FY2023, 10.1% in FY2024, 11.0% in FY2025 and 10.0% in Q3 2026, a short record that has not met a downturn. Free cash flow stability is average: positive in each period but only 40.4% of Adjusted EBITDA. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: USD 1,660 million was refinanced in August 2026 and USD 13.9 billion of loans were sold in nine months, but all eight short-term facilities mature in 2027. Liquidity position is strong: USD 3,049 million of unrestricted cash and USD 2,071 million of issuer-defined availability against USD 71 million drawn. Financial policy and governance is average: supportive conduct with concentrated control. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months management guides only to the end of 2026, with a sequential rise in Q4 retail units and Adjusted EBITDA at the higher end of USD 2.7 billion to USD 3.0 billion, against LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,752 million, and Q4 is seasonally the weakest quarter. Tailwinds are capacity already in place, with the Q3 run rate at 58.0% of stated capacity, and the option to reprice the Term Loan B without the 1.00% premium after 2027-02-14. Headwinds are the 2027 renewals, Ally's commitment ending on 2027-07-26, tax receivable payments rising to about USD 100 million over twelve months, and rising benchmark rates and fuel prices. Over three to five years management targets a retail unit volume 3.45 times the Q3 run rate at a 12.5% operating margin between 2030 and 2035, which needs more reconditioning capacity and is a management goal, not a forecast. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a rise in benchmark rates and wider asset-backed spreads at a time of lower used-car prices, the conditions management already names. The first operational break is the price investors pay for loans: gain per dollar of receivables sold falls further, as it did by about 2.6 percentage points over the past year. The financial transmission is direct because other sales and revenues are all gross profit: two percentage points less gain on the Q3 pace removes USD 412 million a year, and a 10% fall in vehicle gross profit removes USD 312 million more, leaving Adjusted EBITDA at USD 2,028 million, leverage at 2.58x and cash interest cover at 4.33x. Liquidity then depends on whether loan buyers keep buying: if every channel closed, cash plus unused receivable lines would fund about 4.2 months of loan production, and the 2027 facility renewals would fall due in the same period. Management levers are slowing unit growth and inventory purchases, which release working capital, and cutting advertising. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid distress under the earnings shocks alone, and insufficient to absorb a prolonged closure of the loan-sale channel. The observable triggers are gain per dollar sold, the Ally renewal and the 2027 facility extensions. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Carvana presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, growth, low leverage and large cash, but credit quality is constrained by dependence on loan-sale gains, thinning unit profit and concentrated control. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is positive but converts only 40.4% of Adjusted EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the renewal of the 2027 facilities, Ally's commitment and the price investors pay for Carvana's loans. The primary downside path is a loan-sale funding shock that cuts gains and tightens liquidity at the same time. Further analysis would require ratings, loan performance data, the indentures and a maturity ladder after the August 2026 refinancing. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: loan-sale funding stress. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C09; calculation C13

## Gaps

- Minor: The 2026 proxy statement is not supplied. The annual report incorporates by reference the information on directors, executive officers, executive compensation, beneficial ownership, related-party transactions and director independence from it, and the quarterly reports show the 2026 annual meeting has taken place, so the document exists. Business & governance can describe control through the risk factors and equity notes but cannot establish board composition, independence or officer holdings. Adding the proxy statement would close this.

- Minor: Executed debt and financing documents are not supplied, and the run settings declare none. The annual report's exhibit index lists the note indentures, the third-quarter report lists the August 2026 credit agreement as incorporated from a current report, and the floor plan and finance receivable facility agreements are likewise not supplied. Debt terms, guarantees, liens and covenants therefore rest on the filings' note summaries, and Legal & covenants, Covenant capacity, Structural priority, Intercreditor control, Recovery & fulcrum and Security selection cannot be completed from these sources.

- Minor: No principal maturity schedule is printed at 2026-09-30. The only schedule is in the annual report at 2025-12-31 and precedes the August 2026 refinancing that retired the 2030 secured notes and added the Term Loan B, so the maturity wall must be rebuilt from the instrument tables and stated terms, and the real estate financing and the securitization-linked financing have no dated schedule.

- Minor: No issuer credit rating, debt price, spread or peer financial figure is supplied, after searching all seven sources. The annual report mentions rating downgrades only as a generic risk, so rating-based, market-implied and peer-relative work is not supported, and Fundamental credit must state these inputs as not supplied.
- Minor: No document dated after 2026-10-28 is supplied although the as-of date is 2026-11-05, which is eight days later. Any later current report or financing event is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 88; calculation C01

- Minor: Two differences between sources are preserved rather than reconciled. The issuer's availability under short-term facilities is lower than unused commitments; the filing defines availability by pledgeable inventory and finance receivables and does not reconcile the two, so neither is substituted for cash. Share data sit on two bases because a five-for-one split applies in the second- and third-quarter reports and letters but not in the annual report or the first-quarter report and letter, so share counts and per-share figures need conversion before comparison.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 9, 22–24, 78; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-03-31_cvna-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C05; calculation C08

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage is moderate but earnings-dependent: total debt of USD 5,228 million is 1.96x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA and 1.90x Adjusted EBITDA, an improvement that came from earnings growth, not repayment.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 77; calculation C05; calculation C06

### Financial interpretation

Gross leverage on reported EBITDA fell from 4.35x at FY2024 to 2.37x at FY2025 and 1.96x on the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, and the issuer-adjusted measure shows the same path, from 4.09x to 2.29x to 1.90x. Debt did not fall: carrying debt was USD 5,632 million, USD 5,115 million and USD 5,228 million, so the improvement came from Adjusted EBITDA rising from USD 1,378 million to USD 2,237 million and USD 2,752 million on the last twelve months. Because debt edged up after FY2025 and the August 2026 refinancing left gross principal unchanged, creditors' protection depends on EBITDA holding at this level.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C01; calculation C05; calculation C06

The strongest contrary evidence is cash: unrestricted cash rose from USD 1,716 million to USD 2,327 million and USD 3,049 million, so net leverage on reported EBITDA is 3.02x, 1.29x and 0.82x. That view wins only while the cash stays on the balance sheet; working capital can reabsorb it, as inventory growth did with USD 1,025 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 6; calculation C02; calculation C06

Of USD 5,161 million of principal, USD 4,036 million is corporate debt, made up of the 2031 secured notes of USD 2,269 million, the Term Loan B of USD 1,660 million and unsecured notes of USD 107 million, and USD 1,125 million is asset-based funding tied to specific collateral; finance leases of USD 100 million are carried inside debt as well. Floor plan and securitization financing of USD 498 million is matched to inventory and retained interests, so it should not be read as industrial leverage, while the secured notes and Term Loan B of USD 3,929 million rank equally and equal 1.47x reported and 1.43x adjusted EBITDA.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 24–28; calculation C09; calculation C13

The August 2026 refinancing replaced USD 1,660 million of 2030 secured notes with a Term Loan B of the same amount due 2033-08-14, at a cost of USD 50 million of redemption premium and a USD 53 million loss on extinguishment, and left gross principal unchanged. The only printed maturity ladder is at 2025-12-31 and still shows USD 1,708 million due in 2030, so it overstates the 2030 wall and omits the Term Loan B; creditors should read the ladder chart as the position before the refinancing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–27; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 140–141; calculation C08

Cash interest paid was USD 115 million in FY2024, USD 336 million in FY2025 and USD 468 million over the last twelve months, against accrued interest expense, net of USD 651 million, USD 505 million and USD 396 million; the difference is interest paid in kind, USD 458 million in FY2024 and USD 182 million in FY2025, and the 2026 cash flow prints none. Reported EBITDA therefore covers cash interest 11.26x, 6.42x and 5.71x: cover falls although EBITDA grows because interest moved from payment in kind to cash, so the FY2024 ratio overstates debt service capacity.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 103, 166; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 6, 54; calculation C06; calculation C14

Operating cash flow was USD 1,036 million in FY2025 and USD 900 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, after inventory growth of USD 734 million and USD 1,025 million, and with capex of USD 147 million and USD 166 million free cash flow was USD 889 million and USD 734 million. Operating cash flow also carries finance receivable originations of USD 14,187 million in nine months 2026 against USD 14,722 million of sale proceeds, so cash generation depends on continued loan sales as well as on vehicle margins.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C15

Cash of USD 3,049 million is unrestricted, and restricted cash of USD 123 million is separate. Undrawn commitments of USD 5,529 million overstate usable liquidity: the issuer's availability measure, which limits borrowing to pledgeable inventory and finance receivables, is USD 2,071 million, and the seven finance receivable lines fund receivables only through special-purpose subsidiaries. After an October 2026 extension of one line, all eight short-term facilities mature in 2027, the first on 2027-02-14, so renewal is a nearer funding test than the 2031 notes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 78; calculation C07; calculation C17

Two claims sit outside debt. Trade floor plan payables of USD 300 million, up from USD 64 million at 2025-12-31, are interest-bearing inventory financing secured by the financed vehicles but are carried in accounts payable, which rose from USD 1,100 million to USD 1,574 million; adding them lifts leverage on Adjusted EBITDA to 2.01x. The tax receivable agreement liability is USD 2,130 million, and USD 37 million was paid in the nine months to 2026-09-30, so it is a recorded obligation outside debt that reduces cash available to creditors.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 6, 12–13; calculation C12

Reported EBITDA is derived because the issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA. The operating basis is used because a net-income basis would give negative USD 110 million for FY2025 and USD 407 million for the last twelve months, depressed by USD 2,200 million of tax receivable agreement expense, and would put leverage at 12.85x. Adjusted EBITDA exceeds reported EBITDA by only USD 82 million over the last twelve months, which is share-based compensation of USD 97 million in SG&A and USD 4 million in cost of sales and other operating expense of USD 2 million, less warrant revenue of USD 21 million, so the add-backs are small and mostly non-cash.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 80, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 77; calculation C11; calculation C18

The only event after the balance-sheet date is the October 2026 extension of one finance receivable facility from 2026-10-09 to 2027-10-15; it changes neither debt nor cash and is excluded from the period figures. The quarterly report has no subsequent-events note, so no further event is established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23

## Gaps

- Medium: No principal maturity schedule is printed at 2026-09-30. The only ladder is the annual report's at 2025-12-31, which precedes the August 2026 refinancing and still shows USD 1,708 million due in 2030, and the real estate financing, securitization financing and fleet financing have no dated schedule, so a current maturity wall cannot be drawn without estimating. A schedule at 2026-09-30 would close this.

- Medium: Trade floor plan payables of USD 300 million sit in accounts payable and accrued liabilities, outside Total Debt, although the facility is interest-bearing and secured by financed inventory and the payables equal the USD 300 million line. Debt is shown as the issuer classifies it, and the sensitivity is in the calculations; whether lenders treat the payables as debt is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; calculation C12

- Medium: Financial maintenance covenants for the Floor Plan Facility and the finance receivable facilities are not disclosed; the issuer states only that it was in compliance with all debt covenants at 2026-09-30, and the Term Loan B credit agreement has no financial maintenance covenants. Covenant headroom is not established and no capacity is inferred.

- Medium: The legal rank of the floor plan, the finance receivable facilities, the securitization financing, the real estate financing, the fleet financing, the finance leases and the USD 107 million of unsecured notes against the secured notes and the Term Loan B is not stated, so the debt stack shows only the two pari passu secured instruments and cannot support a priority or recovery view. Executed documents would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–28
- Low: The company reports one operating segment, so no segment revenue schedule exists and no segment sum is stated.

- Low: Source dashes stay missing, not zero, in the statement tables, for example other operating expense and loss on debt extinguishment in Q1 and Q2 2026, payment-in-kind interest in nine months 2026 and goodwill at FY2024. Reported totals remain usable; the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation check reads a dash add-back as no amount for that check only.
- Low: Cash taxes paid are printed only for the nine-month periods, not for the fiscal years, so cash tax cover is not calculable for FY2023 to FY2025.
- Low: Capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, and the FY2024 undrawn commitments are printed only as USD 4.1 billion, rounded.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 83, 103

- Low: Stand-alone fourth quarters and discrete Q1 and Q2 2025 columns are not tabulated; the last-twelve-months figures are built from the full year and the nine-month periods, which is the basis the issuer reports.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 6
- Low: Issuance costs on revolving facilities are carried in other assets, not in the debt lines, so carrying debt for those lines is gross of those costs.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

spans.text: ## Request

Business, ownership and transaction fact pack for CARVANA CO. as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, related-party arrangements, financing transactions and the sponsor and governance behaviour evidenced in the FY2025 annual report and the three 2026 quarterly reports, with the three shareholder letters read for management statements.
## Sources

No external source was used. The proxy statement, indentures, credit agreements and subsidiary list are not in the supplied sources.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Carvana's creditors are exposed to loan-sale market access and to related-party contracts as much as to vehicle demand, so funding access and control terms matter more than growth. Gains on loan sales supplied 64.1% of other sales and revenues in Q3 2026, and revenue from related parties supplied 21.9% of them in the nine months to September 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C05; calculation C07

The online used-car retailer is controlled by the Garcia Parties, Ernest Garcia II, Ernest Garcia III and their entities, who held about 83% of the voting power at the 2025 year-end, and a tax receivable agreement liability of USD 2.2 billion, USD 1.7 billion of it owed to related parties, accelerates on a change of control. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium: no dividend or debt-funded distribution is documented and the Garcia Parties committed up to USD 126 million of equity in 2023, but control, related-party dependence and missing ownership detail keep it above Low.
### Key findings

- Loan-sale funding is the dependency that matters most. Gains on loan sales were USD 381 million in Q3 2026, 64.1% of other sales and revenues, which carry a 100% gross margin, and other sales and revenues were 39.4% of gross profit in the nine months to September 2026. Pricing depends on investor demand and credit spreads, so wider spreads would cut gross profit directly. The gain earned per dollar of receivables sold fell from about 10.0% to about 7.4% over the year. Committed capacity is large but finite: the unused commitment of Ally, its committed forward-flow buyer, lasts 9.0 months at the Q3 pace against 9.8 months of remaining term, and USD 8.3 billion of fixed-pool capacity remains.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; calculation C04; calculation C07; calculation C10

- Control rests with one controlling group, and the contracts route services and cash to it. The Garcia Parties hold ten votes per Class B share while their as-exchanged Class A ownership stays at or above 25%, can elect every director and own substantially all of DriveTime. The charter waives their duty to avoid competing businesses. Controlled-company exemptions from board independence rules are available but not used, and holders of LLC units other than Carvana Co. own 34.9% of the operating group.

- The tax receivable agreement is a debt-like claim that competes for cash and accelerates on a change of control. The liability was USD 2,228 million at 2025-12-31, equal to 43.6% of balance-sheet debt at that date, and USD 1,721 million of it was due to related parties. Payments of USD 37 million in the nine months to September 2026 were small, but a merger, breach or early termination makes the obligation immediately payable, and the Senior Secured Notes also carry a change-of-control offer at 101%.

- DriveTime is an embedded related-party provider, and the dependence is rising. Vehicle service contract commissions on contracts administered by DriveTime were USD 349 million in the nine months to September 2026, and revenue from related parties rose from 17.4% of other sales and revenues in FY2024 to 20.0% in FY2025 and 21.9% in the nine months, when it equalled 8.6% of gross profit. DriveTime also administers the limited warranty, services receivables and leases reconditioning centres, and the annual report says these arrangements cannot be assumed to be arm's length.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 124–127; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C08

- The operating model scales with retail units, but unit economics are thinning at the margin. Retail units grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 and retail vehicles reached 75.4% of revenue in the nine months to September 2026 against 71.5% in FY2025, while total gross profit per unit fell by USD 365 to USD 6,997 as loan sale spreads and wholesale profit per unit declined. Management attributes about USD 200 per unit of pressure to fuel prices and rising benchmark rates, and the Q3 run rate uses 58.0% of the retail production capacity management states.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C11

- The August 2026 refinancing cut cost and extended maturity without weakening ranking, but it moved fixed-rate debt to a floating rate. The Term Loan B of USD 1.66 billion is due in 2033, ranks pari passu on first-priority liens and has no financial maintenance covenants. Its effective rate of about 6.1% compares with a 9% cash coupon on the redeemed notes, an indicative saving of USD 48 million a year at the current benchmark, which the management letter says has been rising rapidly.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–27; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C12

- Capital allocation and sponsor conduct have favoured growth, debt reduction and support over payouts. No dividend was paid in FY2025 and no issuer purchase of equity was reported for the fourth quarter. The Garcia Parties committed up to USD 126 million of equity in 2023 and bought units that part-funded a tender offer for the 2025 unsecured notes, USD 539 million of equity was raised in Q3 2025 with no at-the-market sales in 2026, and USD 611 million of 2028 secured notes were repurchased or redeemed in 2025. Acquisitions were small: USD 160 million for five dealerships in 2025 and USD 40 million for two in 2026.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a Medium level is the documented record. No dividend or debt-funded distribution appears in the sources, the Garcia Parties committed up to USD 126 million of equity in 2023, USD 539 million of public equity was raised in Q3 2025, the 2028 secured notes were redeemed early and the August 2026 loan ranks pari passu with no maintenance covenant. Related-party revenue was 8.6% of gross profit in the nine months to September 2026 and related-party payables are only USD 35 million. Loan-sale capacity is committed with four counterparties, Ally for up to USD 8.0 billion and three fixed-pool purchasers for up to USD 12.5 billion in total, and management reports eight consecutive quarters of retail unit growth of about 40%.

The level would fall to Low if the proxy statement showed a board with a majority of independent directors and arm's-length pricing for the DriveTime contracts, and if the indentures limited restricted payments and affiliate transactions tightly. It would rise to High on a distribution, a new unrestricted-subsidiary designation of a core asset, a shortening of the loan-sale commitments, gain on loan sales falling well below the Q3 2026 level, or a sell-down that took the Garcia Parties below the 25% ownership test for ten-vote shares.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement for the 2026 annual meeting is not in the sources, so board independence, sponsor fees and the Garcia Parties' economic ownership are not established, and the Medium sponsor and governance level could move either way once they are known.

- The indentures and credit agreements are not supplied, so the capacity to pay related parties, make distributions or designate unrestricted subsidiaries is not established; the assessment rests on documented behaviour, not on legal capacity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–28
- The terms of the September 2023 exchange offers are not described, so the record of creditor treatment in 2023 is incomplete and may understate creditor-adverse behaviour.

- Loan-sale volumes are printed in rounded billions and the three sale channels are assumed to be additive, so the finding that gain per dollar sold has fallen is approximate and could be narrower or wider.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation C07
- The control percentage is stated only at 2025-12-31, so a change in the Garcia Parties' voting power during 2026 is not established, although Class B share counts did not change.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cvna-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C13
### Company and operating model
| Item | Detail | Source |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The main new debt issue is the Term Loan B of USD 1.66 billion, entered on 2026-08-14 and fully drawn at closing at an issue price of 99.75%. It matures on 2033-08-14, amortises by USD 4 million a quarter from the March 2027 quarter, bears interest at Term SOFR plus 2.25% and ranks pari passu with the Senior Secured Notes on a first-priority lien over substantially all assets. It has no financial maintenance covenants, and a 1.00% premium applies to repricing prepayments until 2027-02-14.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27

The loan proceeds and cash on hand redeemed the 2030 Senior Secured Notes of USD 1,660 million for USD 1,711 million, including a USD 50 million premium and USD 1 million of accrued interest, and Q3 2026 carries a loss on debt extinguishment of USD 53 million. The 2031 Senior Secured Notes of USD 2,269 million remain as the other first-priority instrument, and the refinancing replaced a 9% cash coupon with a loan whose effective rate is about 6.1%.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24–27; calculation C12

Other financing events were smaller. A transportation fleet loan agreement of up to USD 250 million, signed on 2025-10-20, had USD 142 million outstanding at 2026-09-30 against USD 23 million at 2025-12-31. Ally raised its commitment to buy finance receivables to USD 8.0 billion on 2026-07-27, one fixed-pool agreement was increased by USD 500 million in Q3 2026, and one USD 600 million finance receivable facility was extended to October 2027 after the Q3 balance-sheet date. Two franchise dealerships were bought in 2026 for USD 40 million after five in 2025 for USD 160 million, and the Trade Floor Plan Facility that finances their new-vehicle inventory is now USD 300 million.

No sale under the at-the-market program took place in 2026. The five-for-one stock split effected on 2026-05-08 gave each holder four additional shares per share held, so it changed share counts but not ownership proportions.

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for CARVANA CO. as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business, ownership, financial profile, outlook, downside scenario and monitoring view built from the FY2025 annual report, the three 2026 quarterly reports and the three shareholder letters, with the supplied Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses.

No external source was used. Credit ratings, market prices and loan performance data are not in the supplied sources.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Fundamental credit quality is adequate and improving: low leverage and cash balances protect creditors, but earnings depend on loan-sale markets and funding lines that renew during 2027, so a funding shock rather than an earnings fall is the main path to deterioration. Total debt of USD 5,228 million is 1.90x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA and net debt is 0.79x, and two illustrative shocks to loan-sale gains and vehicle profit lift leverage only to 2.58x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C01; calculation C06

The weakest dimension is diversification, because other sales and revenues, which are all gross profit, were 39.4% of nine-month gross profit and depend on investors buying the loans Carvana originates. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium, and the tax receivable agreement, related-party revenue and the 2028 expiry of the rate hedge are the secondary risks.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C02
### Key findings

- Leverage is low and falling because earnings grew, not because debt was repaid. Debt over Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.09x at FY2024 to 2.29x at FY2025 and 1.90x on the last twelve months, while carrying debt moved only from USD 5,632 million to USD 5,115 million and USD 5,228 million. Adjusted EBITDA cover of cash interest is 5.88x, down from 11.98x at FY2024 because interest moved from payment in kind to cash.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C01

- Liquidity is strong today but rests on secured funding capacity that renews in 2027. Unrestricted cash is USD 3,049 million, equal to 58.3% of debt, against USD 71 million drawn on short-term facilities. The eight facilities total USD 5,600 million and 58.9% of that capacity matures by 2027-06-30, so the risk is lost capacity rather than a repayment, while 97.3% of corporate debt is due in 2031 or later.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 78; calculation C07; calculation C08

- Earnings quality hinges on loan-sale gains, and the gain per dollar sold has already fallen. Gains were USD 381 million in Q3 2026, 64.1% of other sales and revenues, and the gain per dollar of receivables sold fell from about 10.0% to about 7.4% in a year, a shortfall of about USD 136 million in the quarter. Each point of gain per dollar is worth USD 206 million a year, 7.5% of Adjusted EBITDA.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation C02; calculation C03

- Unit economics are thinning while volume grows. Total gross profit per retail unit fell by USD 365 to USD 6,997 in Q3 2026 and the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.0% against 11.3%, so at the Q3 run rate that unit decline costs about USD 317 million a year, 11.5% of Adjusted EBITDA. Management attributes about USD 200 per unit of the pressure to fuel prices and rising benchmark rates.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C04

- Stress arithmetic points to funding access, not earnings, as the break point. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against treating funding as the weak point is the record of renewal and growth. Ally's commitment to buy loans rose from USD 4.0 billion in January 2025 to USD 6.0 billion in October 2025 and USD 8.0 billion in July 2026, fixed-pool commitments reached USD 12.5 billion, seven receivable facilities are undrawn, USD 13.9 billion of loans were sold in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and the August 2026 refinancing priced a seven-year loan at a lower cost than the notes it replaced. On that record the funding channel has widened as volume grew, and the shock modelled here would need both a market closure and a fall in gains at once.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–26; calculation C09; calculation C17

The assessment of market access would move from average to strong if the facilities due in 2027 were extended beyond 2027 and Ally's commitment were renewed three months ahead of its 2027-07-26 expiry, as the July 2026 amendment was, with gain per dollar sold holding at about 7.4% or better. It would move to weak if any loan-sale commitment were shortened, if the facility due 2027-02-14 were not extended, if gain per dollar fell below about 5.4%, or if gross profit per unit fell by another USD 365 to about USD 6,632, either of which would move the profile toward the modelled stress level.

### Strengths and weaknesses

Scale and growth are the first strength: retail units grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 while the industry was about flat, and Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 2,752 million over the last twelve months, which supports debt service and lets the company spend on capacity from earnings. Low leverage and large cash are the second: debt is 1.90x Adjusted EBITDA and unrestricted cash is USD 3,049 million, so earnings would have to fall far before debt service is threatened. Long-dated first-lien debt is the third: 97.3% of corporate debt falls due in 2031 or later and the Term Loan B ranks pari passu with the 2031 secured notes, so apart from USD 107 million of unsecured notes there is no corporate maturity wall before 2031. Liquidity is the fourth: USD 2,071 million of availability and USD 4,100 million of unused receivable lines against USD 71 million drawn. A supportive record on payouts is the fifth: no dividend and USD 126 million of sponsor equity in 2023.

Thinning unit profit is the second: gross profit per retail unit fell USD 365 in Q3 2026 and the Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.0% from 11.3%. Funding renewals are the third: 58.9% of the USD 5,600 million of short-term commitments matures by 2027-06-30 and Ally's commitment ends on 2027-07-26. Control and related-party features are the fourth: about 83% of votes with the Garcia Parties and 21.9% of other sales and revenues from DriveTime-related contracts. Claims outside debt are the fifth: a tax receivable agreement of USD 2,230 million that accelerates on a change of control and USD 300 million of trade floor plan payables outside debt.

### Company description

Carvana is an online used-car retailer that sources, reconditions, finances and delivers vehicles through its own network, and it earns profit from three lines. Retail vehicle sales were 75.4% of nine-month revenue but only 49.5% of gross profit, while other sales and revenues, which are loan-sale gains and commissions with no cost of sales, were 39.4% of gross profit. Cash flow therefore depends on retail volume and on investors buying the loans it originates, which makes visibility shorter than the revenue base suggests, and refinancing confidence rests on loan-sale access as much as on vehicle sales. Retail units grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 while the industry was about flat, according to management.

### Ownership and group structure

The Garcia Parties hold about 83% of the voting power through ten-vote Class B shares and own DriveTime, so control and a key counterparty sit with the same group. Carvana Co. owns about 65.1% of the operating group, and the holders of the other units have a tax receivable agreement claim of USD 2,230 million that accelerates on a change of control. Behaviour on record is creditor-supportive, including USD 126 million of equity committed in 2023 and no dividend in FY2025, but the legal capacity to change that is not established, so sponsor and governance risk is Medium.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is volume-driven and discretionary. Retail vehicle sales rose 53.8% in Q3 2026 on 39.4% more units and a higher revenue per unit of USD 28,263 against USD 25,625, a mix of share gains and used-car price appreciation that can reverse. There is no contract revenue: every sale is a one-off transaction with a seven-day return right, and competitors include CarMax, Amazon and DriveTime, which holds a cross-license and could compete. The growth is therefore share gain in a flat industry and not visible recurring revenue, and higher interest rates raise monthly payments and weaken demand.

Margins are defended by scale, not by contract. The Adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.0% in Q3 2026 against 11.3% a year earlier, so growth of 39.4% in units did not stop it falling by 1.3 percentage points. SG&A was USD 805 million in the quarter, of which advertising was USD 152 million and compensation USD 255 million, both linked to volume, while fixed and variable cost shares are not disclosed. Management attributes USD 365 of lower gross profit per unit to loan pricing given back to customers and lower wholesale profit, so margin holds under volume pressure only if loan-sale spreads hold.

### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense but fragmented: the ten largest used-car retailers held less than 10% of the market in 2024 and Carvana has about 2% of it, so share gains can continue, while price competition from CarMax, Amazon and franchise dealers limits margin. New entrants face high operating complexity in reconditioning and logistics, though technology changes such as artificial intelligence and autonomous vehicles are cited as risks to the model. Buyer power is high because switching costs are low and returns are allowed for seven days. Supplier power matters most in funding: vehicles come from customers, auctions and fleets, but Ally and the loan buyers decide how much Carvana can sell, and commercial suppliers review their disposition channels through requests for proposals.

Economic factors are a primary credit driver because benchmark rates and used-car prices set loan-sale pricing and affordability: management reports rapidly rising benchmark rates and fuel prices that cost about USD 200 per unit in Q3 2026. Regulators scrutinise advertising, financing and insurance in used-vehicle sales, which could narrow Carvana's differentiation, and the quarterly report says tariffs and the conflict involving Iran did not materially affect Q3 results. ### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are scale and growth, low leverage with large cash, and long-dated first-lien corporate debt, which together give creditors a margin of safety today. Weaknesses are dependence on loan-sale gains, thinning unit profit, and control and related-party features. The main opportunity is renewal of the 2027 facilities and Ally's commitment on longer terms, which would remove the nearest funding test and lift the profile. The main threats are wider loan-sale spreads, a fall in used-car prices that creates markdown risk on inventory, and a change of control that would accelerate the tax receivable agreement.

### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position is strong: retail units grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 and the business has about 2% of the used market, which leaves large room for share gains but shows it is far from dominant. Competitive advantage is average: management says its margins are about twice the industry average, but switching costs are low and rivals can copy the online model. Business diversification is weak: a single market, the United States, one online channel and one product category, with other sales and revenues tied to retail units and to loan buyers. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capex is only 0.7% of revenue and advertising can be cut, but the fixed cost share is not disclosed. Margin stability is average: the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 3.1% in FY2023, 10.1% in FY2024, 11.0% in FY2025 and 10.0% in Q3 2026, a short record that has not met a downturn. Free cash flow stability is average: positive in each period but only 40.4% of Adjusted EBITDA. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: USD 1,660 million was refinanced in August 2026 and USD 13.9 billion of loans were sold in nine months, but all eight short-term facilities mature in 2027. Liquidity position is strong: USD 3,049 million of unrestricted cash and USD 2,071 million of issuer-defined availability against USD 71 million drawn. Financial policy and governance is average: supportive conduct with concentrated control.

The main supports are liquidity and falling leverage; the constraints are diversification and funding dependence; the trend is improving on earnings but softening on unit profit; and the missing data are ratings, loan performance and a post-refinancing maturity ladder.
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months management guides only to the end of 2026, with a sequential rise in Q4 retail units and Adjusted EBITDA at the higher end of USD 2.7 billion to USD 3.0 billion, against LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,752 million, and Q4 is seasonally the weakest quarter. Tailwinds are capacity already in place, with the Q3 run rate at 58.0% of stated capacity, and the option to reprice the Term Loan B without the 1.00% premium after 2027-02-14. Headwinds are the 2027 renewals, Ally's commitment ending on 2027-07-26, tax receivable payments rising to about USD 100 million over twelve months, and rising benchmark rates and fuel prices. Over three to five years management targets a retail unit volume 3.45 times the Q3 run rate at a 12.5% operating margin between 2030 and 2035, which needs more reconditioning capacity and is a management goal, not a forecast.

### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a rise in benchmark rates and wider asset-backed spreads at a time of lower used-car prices, the conditions management already names. The first operational break is the price investors pay for loans: gain per dollar of receivables sold falls further, as it did by about 2.6 percentage points over the past year. The financial transmission is direct because other sales and revenues are all gross profit: two percentage points less gain on the Q3 pace removes USD 412 million a year, and a 10% fall in vehicle gross profit removes USD 312 million more, leaving Adjusted EBITDA at USD 2,028 million, leverage at 2.58x and cash interest cover at 4.33x. Liquidity then depends on whether loan buyers keep buying: if every channel closed, cash plus unused receivable lines would fund about 4.2 months of loan production, and the 2027 facility renewals would fall due in the same period. Management levers are slowing unit growth and inventory purchases, which release working capital, and cutting advertising. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid distress under the earnings shocks alone, and insufficient to absorb a prolonged closure of the loan-sale channel. The observable triggers are gain per dollar sold, the Ally renewal and the 2027 facility extensions.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Carvana presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, growth, low leverage and large cash, but credit quality is constrained by dependence on loan-sale gains, thinning unit profit and concentrated control. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is positive but converts only 40.4% of Adjusted EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the renewal of the 2027 facilities, Ally's commitment and the price investors pay for Carvana's loans. The primary downside path is a loan-sale funding shock that cuts gains and tightens liquidity at the same time. Further analysis would require ratings, loan performance data, the indentures and a maturity ladder after the August 2026 refinancing. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: loan-sale funding stress.
